title: Daylight Lab: A browser-based daylight simulation tool
description:
Daylight Lab is a daylighting analysis tool for architecture students that runs entirely in the browser. It ships as a single self-contained HTML file with no CDN, no build step for the end user and no install.

A parametric room is modelled with real wall, roof and floor thickness; windows, skylights and doors can be added, sized and moved; horizontal and vertical shading devices are supported. A 3D sun path shows shadows and visible solar rays, and a workplane grid reports illuminance, daylight factor and useful daylight illuminance, together with daylight autonomy, spatial daylight autonomy, annual sunlight exposure and direct sun hours.

Two independent engines are provided: a Monte-Carlo raytracer using daylight coefficients over Tregenza/Reinhart sky patches, and a BRE split-flux implementation following BS 8206-2. Their agreement is measured and published in docs/ENGINE-VALIDATION.md. The method notes in docs/method-notes.html document every assumption, name every source the code implements, and declare the tool's limitations.
